Paul Strauss

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, District of Columbia · Incumbent

U.S. Shadow Senator for the District of Columbia; attorney

Paul Strauss is a Democrat who has served as the District of Columbia's U.S. Shadow Senator, a non-voting position listed on the ballot as United States Senator, since January 1997. He is seeking a sixth six-year term. Reports say he was unopposed in the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary after Markus Batchelor was denied ballot access, and he faces Republican Robert Simmons in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Strauss stands

DC statehood
Supports admitting the District of Columbia as the 51st state. He advocates in the U.S. Senate and House for DC residents' full federal representation and self-determination.
Congressional representation for DC
Supports full voting representation in Congress for DC residents and greater self-government for the District.

Background

  • U.S. Shadow Senator, District of Columbia, 1997–present (term ends January 3, 2027)
  • Attorney in private practice
  • Adjunct professor, American University Department of Government
  • J.D., American University
  • Superdelegate from DC at the 2016 Democratic National Convention

Also running for United States Senator

  • Robert Simmons Republican
